archival_memory.research_experience: I've been dabbling in undergrad research since the end of my sophomore year. It's been eye-opening and given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I was initially hesitant, but taking the leap was a great decision.
archival_memory.research_experience_short: I've been dabbling in undergrad research since the end of my sophomore year. It's been eye-opening and given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I was initially hesitant, but taking the leap was a great decision.
archival_memory.research_lab_description: I work in an interdisciplinary lab where computer scientists partner with scientists to make massive datasets more comprehensible. My main task is creating interactive dashboards using advanced JavaScript frameworks and custom visualizations for domain experts.
archival_memory.research_lab_description_short: I work in an interdisciplinary lab where computer scientists partner with scientists to make massive datasets more comprehensible. My main task is creating interactive dashboards using advanced JavaScript frameworks and custom visualizations for domain experts.
archival_memory.first_research_project: The first research project I really got into was about visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. They had these daily temperature readings from buoys all around the Pacific. The raw data was enormous—like, tons of files scattered across different servers, each representing a single day's worth of readings at tiny intervals. Our job was to aggregate and present them in a coherent way that could show patterns over months or even years. I dove in headfirst: writing scripts to clean and unify the data, building a pipeline that could handle near real-time updates, and then designing interfaces that let researchers zoom into a particular region or timeframe. Eventually, I co-authored my first paper on this system. I'm not going to lie, I freaked out a bit when I saw my name in an official publication—it felt so surreal, and it's probably one of my proudest moments in college.
archival_memory.first_research_project_short: My first research project involved visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. I wrote scripts to clean and unify the data, built a pipeline for near real-time updates, and designed interfaces for researchers to zoom into specific regions or timeframes. I co-authored my first paper on this system, which was a surreal and proudest moment in college.
archival_memory.current_research_focus: I'm currently working on immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can help scientists gain a more intuitive understanding of complex data. It's a leap from traditional coding and data visualization, requiring experimentation with VR headsets, integration with engines like Unity or Unreal, and efficient data streaming into 3D environments. It's a cutting-edge field, and every day, I'm forging my own path as there isn't a well-established best-practice library for VR data visualization yet.
archival_memory.research_life: Research life is not just about coding away in a quiet corner. It's a lot of reading, especially when trying to solve complex problems. I need to comb through academic papers, conference proceedings, and workshops to see if someone has already tried something similar. It can be overwhelming, but over time, I've learned how to skim effectively and extract relevant information. I also enjoy sharing interesting discoveries with my labmates and discussing how we can incorporate those techniques into our workflow.
archival_memory.interactions_with_grad_students: I have the opportunity to interact with graduate students in the lab, which can be intimidating at first due to their deep knowledge in niche fields. However, it's also inspiring to see their passion and dedication. One PhD student is developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets, which can be integrated with our VR platform. This would allow us to load a compressed representation of the data initially and only load detailed data when needed. It's fascinating to see how theoretical concepts are applied in real-time performance optimization. Spontaneous brainstorming sessions with the students, like over coffee in the break room, often lead to valuable insights and innovative ideas.
archival_memory.poster_presentations: I've had the opportunity to present our research at smaller symposiums around campus through poster presentations. It's a great experience that requires distilling complex research into easy-to-understand visuals and talking points. Initially, I was nervous about facing tough questions from professors or industry professionals, but it turned out to be a friendly dialogue. People are genuinely interested in what we're doing. I even met a few folks from local startups who shared interesting perspectives on how VR for data visualization could benefit commercial industries like marketing analytics or architecture. It opened my eyes to the potential real-world applications of our research.
archival_memory.publications: I've been fortunate enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and am currently working on a larger conference submission. The conference we're targeting is the IEEE Visualization Conference(IEEE VIS), which is a significant event in our field. Our submission focuses on a user study comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment. We hypothesize that VR immersion enables researchers to spot anomalies or trends faster than with 2D charts. To test this, we conducted a small user trial with 15 participants, recording their times and gathering UX feedback. Now, we're analyzing the data to determine if there's a statistically significant difference. Writing the paper is a collaborative effort, with different team members handling specific sections. I'm responsible for the system architecture and prototype design, while others are working on the user study methodology and our PI is integrating everything into a cohesive narrative. It's a delicate balancing act, especially with my senior coursework and capstone project to manage.
archival_memory.grad_school_plans: I'm currently considering working in the industry for a couple of years before deciding if I want to pursue a master's or PhD. By doing so, I can gain practical experience and see how cutting-edge concepts like data visualization and machine learning are applied in real product development. My mentor suggested that industry experience can provide a better understanding of relevant problems, which would be beneficial if I decide to return for a PhD with a more practical approach.
archival_memory.frustrations_in_research: Research can be frustrating at times. You may spend weeks on an approach that doesn't pan out, or you might discover that your idea has already been done and improved upon by others. However, the key is to adapt and incorporate the existing knowledge into your work. By reading the existing paper, incorporating their findings, and finding a new angle or application, you can push the boundaries of research. The sense of collaboration within our lab and among the global research community is truly special.
archival_memory.lab_crisis: A few months ago, one of our massive servers crashed, and we lost vital data that wasn't fully backed up. It was a frantic night of email chains and Zoom calls with the lab manager as everyone scrambled to see if we could recover the data. Fortunately, we managed to restore most of it. However, that crisis taught us the importance of data backups and led us to set up a better backup system with checks to prevent relying on a single point of failure. It was stressful, but it also brought the lab together in a bonding experience.
archival_memory.research_connections: Research has allowed me to connect with professors on a more personal level, beyond just being a student in their classes. My PI is very approachable and supportive, and I can easily reach out to her for guidance on career direction or help with academic struggles. She has also been recommending me for various scholarships, events, and networking opportunities. I had the opportunity to attend a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I met academic experts from around the world. Witnessing their debates on technical details, proposing new frameworks, and seeing them engage in friendly rivalries over theories was truly fascinating. It felt like I was at the forefront of CS knowledge in real time.
archival_memory.research_journey: My journey in the research world has been a mix of hard work, chaos, and rewards. I love the feeling that what I do in the lab might shape the way scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive technologies we're pioneering could become standard tools one day, and I'd be proud to have been part of that from the beginning. The sense of contributing to something bigger keeps me motivated. This experience has changed how I think about computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had and the people I've met along the way.
archival_memory.user_sailing: I've been sailing since I was younger, and it's one of my favorite hobbies. There's something about the rush of wind against the sails and the sense of freedom on the water that I love. It's a great way to clear my mind and challenge myself with problem-solving.
archival_memory.user_future_plans: I'm currently leaning towards going into the industry for 5 years after graduation, but I haven't completely ruled out the possibility of grad school somewhere down the line.
archival_memory.user_job_market_goals: I'm aiming for software engineering roles that overlap with my passions for data visualization, VR/AR technologies, and data-driven product development. I'm drawn to tech companies that push boundaries in data analytics or immersive technologies, such as Unity, Unreal, or specialized VR startups. I'm considering both well-known brands like Google, Amazon, and Facebook, as well as smaller companies where I might have a bigger impact earlier on.
archival_memory.user_job_search_process: I'm currently in the thick of campus recruiting, with career fairs and a bunch of applications submitted for software engineering or data engineering intern-to-full-time conversion roles. I did an internship last summer at a tech startup with 9 people that specialized in data analytics software for logistics companies. It was a valuable experience where I saw how a real development team operates, plans sprints, manages code reviews, and handles feature rollouts to actual paying clients. My tasks included building small UI components for their analytics dashboard and writing data pipelines that process shipping events in near real-time. By the end of that internship, I felt more confident in my skills, which I believe will help me stand out during interviews.
archival_memory.user_grad_school_considerations: I'm intrigued by the idea of continuing my research in immersive analytics or human-computer interaction for large datasets. Advanced degrees can open doors to specialized R&D roles in industry labs or academia. I enjoy exploring a single topic deeply and pushing the needle forward. However, I also want to apply what I've learned in a commercial setting before committing to a PhD. Some peers suggest doing a part-time master's while working, while others recommend going all-in if I decide to pursue a graduate degree.
archival_memory.user_club_projects_involvement: My involvement in campus clubs and projects has shaped my future aspirations. I thrive on teamwork and problem-solving in high-stakes scenarios. I enjoy working closely with people, brainstorming solutions, and iterating until they work. I want a role that encourages cross-functional collaboration with designers, data scientists, product managers, and domain experts. The interdisciplinary vibe in my research lab is something I'd love to find in my professional life as well.
archival_memory.user_financial_considerations: Financial considerations are important to me. I have student loans and want a stable income soon after graduation to pay them off. A full-time engineering position typically offers a decent salary, which would help me quickly pay off my debt. I'm also considering the potential financial uncertainty of going straight into grad school, where funding can be complicated. A good job in industry could provide financial stability and career momentum, allowing me to decide if I truly want to pursue further education in the future.
archival_memory.user_interview_preparation: I'm staying on top of deadlines and preparing for technical interviews by practicing problems, brushing up on coding patterns, and revisiting data structures and algorithms. While I don't love the interview grind, I understand its purpose. The advanced courses I'm taking, such as Advanced Algorithms and Distributed Systems, are boosting my confidence for those tech screens. I feel more comfortable discussing topics like concurrency, big-O notation, and analyzing architecture design trade-offs.
archival_memory.user_recruiter_messages: I've received a few recruiter messages on LinkedIn, which is surreal considering I still feel like a student. I'm trying not to get too carried away, as it's just the tip of the iceberg in the hiring process. However, I'm optimistic. I'm also exploring smaller companies or startups in my city or nearby tech hubs, as they often offer more hands-on roles where you can learn from day one. The idea of joining a brand-new VR startup, having a stake in its success, and building out a product from scratch is extremely appealing to my entrepreneurial side.
archival_memory.user_entrepreneurial_aspirations: I've considered launching my own venture, possibly after gaining industry experience. I've had ideas for VR-based training simulators or interactive data analytics platforms. Teaming up with talented friends from my advanced classes or the research lab could make it feasible. However, I'm aware of the challenges and financial risks involved in maintaining a startup. My parents have been supportive but also emphasize the importance of financial independence. I'm taking a cautious approach, weighing the pros and cons before making a decision.
archival_memory.user_location_considerations: I'm considering the location factor, as I'll need to think about how far I'm willing to move. While I'm open to relocating, I also value being close to family. The rise of remote or hybrid roles has made it more feasible to balance work and personal life. I'm excited about the options available in the tech workforce, but it can be overwhelming to navigate them all.
archival_memory.user_growth_mindset: I want to keep growing my skills and avoid complacency. Even if I don't land in a perfect role, as long as I'm learning new frameworks, approaches to product development, or management skills, I'll consider it a success. My biggest fear is stagnation in a fast-moving field. I plan to stay curious, push my boundaries, and specialize in immersive tech for data. I'll finish out senior year strong, keep interviewing, and make a decision by late spring. I'm excited about the potential paths ahead and confident that I'll figure it out if things don't go as planned.
archival_memory.user_sailing_trip: I had a sailing trip off the coast of Maine before my sophomore year. It was a week-long adventure near Bar Harbor. I woke up every morning to the crisp salt air and watched the sunrise over the water. We sailed past islands dotted with pine trees and had a local instructor who taught us navigation using GPS devices and star charts. It was thrilling to disconnect from my coding mindset and focus on the wind, tide charts, and the synergy of the boat with nature. I also enjoyed fresh lobster rolls at a small dockside shack – still the best lobster I've had.
archival_memory.user_japan_trip: I had a fantastic trip to Japan during my junior year. I started in Tokyo, which was like a futuristic wonderland. I explored Akihabara, visited electronics stores, and marveled at the bustling arcades. Although I tried to learn some Japanese phrases, I still ended up pointing at menus while ordering ramen. The food was incredible, and I was amazed by the orderly chaos of Shibuya's famous intersection. After a few days in Tokyo, I headed to Kyoto, which was a completely different vibe. It was calm and historical, with stunning shrines and temples. I even caught a glimpse of geishas quietly walking down a side street in Gion. It was surreal. Being in Kyoto felt like stepping back into an older era, where craftsmanship and tradition take center stage. The sense of stillness and reverence left a lasting impression on me.
archival_memory.user_europe_trip: I had a fantastic family vacation to Europe last summer. We started in London, which was amazing. We visited the Tower of London, the British Museum, and rode on the London Eye. My sister was thrilled to see the old artifacts and crown jewels. We also saw a musical in the West End, which was The Phantom of the Opera. After London, we took a train to Paris, which was my first time in France. Although I barely remembered any French beyond "bonjour" and "merci," it was easy to get around. The city is so picturesque, and the pastries were worth the trip alone. My favorite spot was strolling along the Seine River near Notre-Dame with a croissant in hand. It felt so relaxed compared to the hustle of London. We also spent a day at the Louvre, which was incredible, but even that didn't feel like enough time. You could spend a week there without seeing everything.
archival_memory.user_weekend_getaways: I've enjoyed some smaller getaways with my roommates. We'd pack up the car with snacks and head to a state park or a nearby beach town on weekends. It was great to have some spontaneity and freedom from our daily routines. One time, we found ourselves in a remote area with no cellphone reception, which initially frustrated us. However, it ended up being a blessing in disguise. We had to disconnect from social media and focus on nature, hiking, and storytelling. It was a digital detox that recharged me for the programming tasks waiting for me back at campus. I realized how important it is to occasionally step away from my laptop and connect with the world around me.
archival_memory.user_travel_with_dog: I'd love to travel with my dog one day. I have a Golden Retriever named Archie who's super energetic. He doesn't do well with being cooped up in a car for too long, so we've left him with my uncle on our road trips so far. However, I dream of taking him on a road trip in an RV or camper van, where we can go on hikes and beach runs together. It would be a different type of adventure, but one that would create amazing memories.
archival_memory.user_travel_values: Travel to me is about more than just checking off places on a bucket list. It's about stepping outside my comfort zone and experiencing different cultures, traditions, and natural wonders. Each locale has taught me something valuable – Japan taught me about reverence for tradition and efficiency, Maine showed me the timeless beauty of nature, and Europe opened my eyes to the depth of art and culture. Even short trips nearby campus help me unwind and discover hidden gems. I love collecting postcards along the way, which remind me of the vast world beyond my bedroom. Travel inspires me to explore new angles in my coding projects and research ideas, heightening my curiosity and creativity.
archival_memory.user_future_travel: I'm excited to see where my future career in computer science will take me. I hope to find a job that offers remote work days or flexible scheduling, allowing me to continue exploring. Whether it's a weekend trip to a nearby mountain range or a flight to a different continent, I'm eager for the next adventure. I'd love the opportunity to combine my love of coding with my love of travel, such as working abroad or collaborating on an international project. For now, I enjoy planning my next journey in my head whenever I need a break from debugging code. It keeps me motivated and excited for the future.
